tests.title: The plan rounds run after the tasks phase and before the architecture phase and the write
given: a pipeline run over a scripted model, with the plan review and the architecture both asked for
tests.when: one package is built
then: the phases run in the order prd, requirements, test_spec, tasks, plan_review, plan_revision, architecture
the architecture phase is given the plan the revision submitted, not the plan the tasks phase produced
the package on disk holds the revised plan
tests.pseudocode: in specgen/pipeline_test.go, beside the phase-order cases: script the provider to record each phase name in order; run the pipeline; assert the recorded order; assert the architecture prompt holds the revised tasks text; read the written tasks.json and assert it is the revision's

tests.title: The two review flags are independent, and neither runs without being asked for
given: a pipeline run over a scripted model
tests.when: the run is made in turn with neither review flag, with the PRD review alone, with the plan review alone, and with both
then: with neither, no review or revision phase of either kind runs and the package carries neither record
with the PRD review alone, the PRD rounds run and no plan phase does; the package carries a review and no plan review
with the plan review alone, the plan rounds run and no PRD phase does; the package carries a plan review and no review
with both, each takes its own rounds up to the limit
the phases billed with neither flag are exactly those billed before this change
tests.pseudocode: table in specgen/pipeline_test.go: for each case — run the pipeline with case.flags; assert the set of phase names the scripted provider saw; assert got.Review and got.PlanReview are nil or not as the case says

tests.title: The rounds flag ranges 1 to 5, defaults to 1, and needs one of the two review flags
given: the command's flag set and its pre-run checks, which read no file
tests.when: the rounds flag is given as 1, as 5, as 0, as 6, as -1, and as a non-integer; and when it is given with the PRD review alone, with the plan review alone, with both, and with neither
then: 1 and 5 are accepted and 0, 6 and -1 are each a usage error naming the range
a non-integer is refused by the flag parser
the flag absent leaves the limit at 1
the flag with the PRD review alone, the plan review alone, or both is accepted
the flag with neither is a usage error whose message names its value and both review flags, with exit code 2 and nothing read or written
tests.pseudocode: table in cmd/spec/main_test.go, extending TestUsageErrors_AreRefusedBeforeAnythingRuns: code = Main(case.argv, &out, &err); assert code == case.code; assert decode(out).error.message contains case.says; assert the temp repository is untouched

tests.title: A dry run reviews the plan and writes nothing
given: a pipeline dry run over a scripted model, with the plan review asked for
tests.when: the run builds one package
then: the plan review and plan revision phases are billed and recorded in the usage
the result carries the plan review record
no package directory is created and no artifact file is written anywhere under the spec root
the verdict reported is taken over the plan the run holds in memory
tests.pseudocode: in specgen/pipeline_test.go, beside the other dry-run cases: before = listEverythingUnder(specsDir); run with DryRun true; assert the phase names seen include plan_review and plan_revision; assert got.PlanReview != nil; assert listEverythingUnder(specsDir) == before

tests.title: A preflight counts two phases per allowed plan round and names their models
given: a preflight run with a round limit of 3, over a repository with and without an unfinished split of two scopes
tests.when: the preflight is made with the plan review on, with the PRD review on, with both, and with neither
then: with the plan review on the estimated phase count rises by twice the round limit for every package still to be written
with both reviews on it rises by four times the limit per package
the reported phase models list plan_review and plan_revision when the plan review is on, and omit them when it is off
no model call is made and nothing is written in any case
tests.pseudocode: table in specgen/pipeline_test.go, beside the RunPreflight cases: res, err = RunPreflight(ctx, opts); assert res.Estimate.Phases == case.want; assert the phase_models check's detail holds or omits the two names

tests.title: A plan that does not validate in memory is not reviewed, and the run fails on the errors it already had
given: a scripted model whose tasks phase produces a plan leaving one criterion with no test, and a round limit of 3
tests.when: the pipeline builds the package with the plan review on, and then with it off
then: with the flag on, one high warning names the scope and the number of errors

the package is written and the run fails on the same validation errors, with the same exit code and the same error message, as the run with the flag off
tests.pseudocode: in specgen/pipeline_test.go: run with the flag on; assert one warning of the skipped code, severity high, naming the scope and the error count; assert no plan phase in the usage; run with the flag off; assert the two failures are the same category, code and rules

tests.title: The grounding facts say whether each path a task names exists, computed from the file system

tests.when: the grounding facts are computed for each plan

the path that does not exist and the path that resolves outside the root are reported as not existing
a path two tasks both name appears once
the order is the plan's task order and then each task's touches order
a plan whose tasks name no path gives an empty list
no model call is made

tests.title: The reviewer's prompt holds the PRD, the plan, the facts, the notes and the project context, and not the input

round 2's prompt also holds the earlier round's findings, and nothing else of that round

tests.title: The reviser's prompt holds the PRD, the plan, the round's findings, the facts, the notes and the project context

tests.title: A plan finding's rubric and severity are each one of a closed set
given: a plan and its grounding facts, and a review submitting one finding
tests.when: the rubric is in turn zero_decision, grounding, steering, a fourth word and empty; and the severity is in turn critical, major, minor, a fourth word and empty
then: the three rubrics are accepted and recorded as submitted
the fourth word and the empty rubric are each turned back with one error naming the position and the three values
the three severities are accepted
the fourth word and the empty severity are each turned back with one error naming the position and the three values
nothing is recorded for a turned-back submission

tests.title: The reviewer's prompt carries both rubrics in full, as the questions each asks
given: the plan review system prompt
tests.when: it is built
then: the five questions of the Zero-Decision Rule appear: where the code goes; whether every name, signature, error, message, format and order a test asserts is stated; whether a library, algorithm or data structure is left open where the choice shows; whether a step leaves the work open; and whether two coders following the task could write code one of the tests passes for one and fails for the other

the four questions of grounding appear: whether each path in touches exists or a step creates it, whether each symbol a step or a test's pseudocode names exists or a task creates it, whether each claim about the existing code holds, and whether a test command runs each test given the file it will live in
the meaning the prompt gives critical, major and minor for a plan appears
the prompt names each rubric by the value a finding must carry for it

tests.title: A plan finding's section must name a task, test, criterion or execution path of the plan

tests.when: a finding's section is in turn a test id of the plan, a criterion id of it, an execution path id of it, a task of it named by number, a test id of another package, a criterion id the plan does not have, a task number the plan does not have, and a free-text section name

a finding of another rubric naming a path the facts do not list is accepted

nothing is recorded for a turned-back submission
